body:
Found by review of getwyrd/wyrd-pdca#253 (the v0.58.0 upgrade), which retired the instance's own wait for #462's `_wait_for_green`. The instance's wait had one extra step that upstream's lacks, and the review asked for it back.

## Problem

`_wait_for_green` re-reads the rollup only while it is `pending` or `empty`. During the seconds in which a freshly opened PR's checks are registering, the rollup does not say "incomplete": it reports whatever has registered SO FAR. One fast workflow that has already passed (a DCO check, an issue-linkage check) reads as a clean green while the slow job that matters has not created its check run yet. `_merge_one` then merges on that partial green. Where the slow job is a host-required check, `gh pr merge` refuses and the wave stops (a routine stop the wait exists to avoid); where it is not required — exactly the thin-branch-protection case the full-rollup gate under `merge_requires = "all"` covers — the PR merges and the check fails afterwards on the base.

The same applies to a green reached through the loop (`empty → green`): the first read after the wait can be just as partial.

## Fix the instance carries

Confirm a green once: re-read it one poll interval later and believe it only if it held. A re-read that went `pending`/`empty` falls back into the wait; `failing`/`unreadable` returns at once. `wait_secs <= 0` stays a single read. The confirm is charged to the budget, so a small `merge_wait_secs` cannot sleep longer than the operator allowed. `test_pending_then_green_merges` then sees four rollup reads (pending, pending, green, green) instead of three.
title: merge: _wait_for_green believes the first green — a fast check can pass before a slow one has registered
